utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I please seek leave to present a public summary of the witness's evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Mirza Sabljica served as a forensic ballistics analyst with the security services centre, for CSB, in Sarajevo from July 1993. He participated in ballistic investigations of shelling and sniping incidents in Sarajevo. The witness describes the methodology used when investigating incidents, including the method of determining the calibre of the projectile, the direction of fire, and the angle of descent at the point of impact. He also discusses documentary evidence prepared by his team and others relating to a number of shelling and sniping incidents, including the shelling of a football game in Dobrinja on the 1st of June, 1993; the shelling of a civilian location where a group of children were playing in the snow on the 22nd of January, 1994; the shelling of a residential area in Dobrinja on the 4th of February, 1994; and the shelling of the Markale Market on the 5th of February, 1994. In respect of the Markale Market incident, Mr. Sabljica describes the work done upon his arrival at the scene of the shelling after the shelling had taken place, including the measurement of the shell crater and inspection of the traces on the ground. He concluded on the basis of his measurements that the projectile had come from a north/north-eastern direction at a bearing of approximately 18 degrees. In respect of the shelling on the 22nd of January, 1994, Mr. Sabljica's statement refers to his report of the incident, in which he concluded that the projectiles had been fired from positions in Nedzarici, an area which was under Bosnian Serb control. Mr. Sabljica also participated in approximately 60 investigations into incidents of sniping. Among the sniping incidents he discusses are a sniping attack on the tram on the 23rd of November, 1994. He states that the origin of the sniper fire often was the Metaljka building and other high-rise buildings in Grbavica, an area under Bosnian Serb control. That concludes the witness summary. At this time may I proceed with questioning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, thank you for your patience. On pages 10 to 18 of your statement you explain the process of ballistics analysis you used during your 80 to a hundred investigations of shelling incidents. Before we discuss some specific investigations, I would like to discuss with you some general items. On page 11 of your statement you explain that when you arrived on scene you looked at: "Mechanical traces resulting from impact of projectiles and fragments and that would be contoured on an asphalt surface or some other surface." Could you please explain to us the visible traces left by a projectile on an asphalt surface or other surface?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: In the course of the fall of a projectile - in this case a shell - the body of the shell will burst and the fragments will usually leave an identical trace on the surface, which is known as a rosetta. In other words, around the centre of the crater there would be two irregular ellipses that fan out and stretch upwards -- or rather, they are most visible in the direction from which the projectile actually came.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you describe a rosetta, are you referring to a particular type of shell or a pattern caused by a particular type of shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. At the very start of my sentence, that's what I said. This is typical of shells, mortar shells, in other words, from smooth barrels, and these projectiles leave a very characteristic pattern which is known under the name of rosetta.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your statement you indicate that you used the central axis method to determine the direction of fire. Could you please explain this method.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. Based on the traces found, I mean these two ellipses, regular ellipses that are formed around the centre of the crater, we would then connect the points of the axis of the longer ellipse with the centre of the pattern; and then you get an angle and a middle axis that would determine the direction from which the projectile had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would you use any particular type of equipment in performing this analysis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, is these explanations, is there any way to visualise them?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I will be going through photos if you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if the witness now explains if it's visible on the photos, rather use the photos now so that we do not miss part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before going to specific incident, on page 14 of your statement you stated: "Based on the size of damage because an 82-millimetre creates a smaller damage than created by a 120-millimetre shell ..." During your investigations could you tell the difference in calibre based upon observations of the impact site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, of course. An 82-millimetre weapon, the rosetta or those ellipses would be smaller of course than the ones created or that left behind a 120-millimetre shell. Of course that would also depend on the surface of impact, but usually the differences that we would get during these regiments -- measurements would be about 30 per cent less; in other words, when you compare the two shells, the 80-millimetre and 120-millimetre traces, it's easy to actually identify which calibre is in question based on these different sizes of the crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 10261, page 3, in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On pages 18 and 19 of your statement, you provide evidence concerning your investigation of the shelling of Dobrinja on 1 June 1993. On page 19 you confirm the authenticity of a report authored by yourself and Mr. Zlatko Medjedovic. Is this the report you were referring to in your statement that is now before you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that is the report that me and the late Zlatko Medjedovic actually put together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 6 of the B/C/S version only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your report you make a number of forensic observations and refer to photographs. Directing your attention to the top photograph marked number 3, in your report you refer to this photograph and state: "The centre of the crater shows physical damage to the Tarmac surface and is in the shape of an irregular circle ..." And: "The central part of the crater spreads out in traces of elliptical rays or, specifically, the centre of the explosion is surrounded by two ellipses." Could you please explain to us using this photo the two ellipses and what they show?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: May I use this pen?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would not affect the integrity of the exhibit as a whole. So, yes, then the witness -- Mr. Usher, could you guide the witness in what pen to use.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to try and illustrate the entire methodology we used based on this photograph. As the Prosecutor asked about the central crater and it has the shape of an irregular circle, this is it. Now, around it there would be two irregular ellipses, this is one of them and this is the second one. So as I've said before, portions, fragments, of very hot metal would -- coming from the disintegrated shell would form this pattern on the Tarmac surface. Now, here we have the axis of these ellipses and we can see that the traces are more visible and deeper and they spread out at a distance from the -- away from the direction from which the shell came. Now, we can see next to this that there is a measuring tape which is part of our forensic equipment used in measuring the dimensions or size of the trace evidence found, physical evidence found on a Tarmac surface.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you for a second. Could you perhaps using a small arrow first put a C for centre to the first irregular circle you've drawn.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you make E1 and E2, E1 for the smaller ellipse and the E2 pointing at the borders for the larger ellipse.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then we have two X's. Could you indicate what is X1 and what is X2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here we have the longer, it would be X1 and the shorter one X2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With respect to the larger ellipse that you've drawn which is now marked E2, what specifically does this ellipse show?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'm not receiving interpretation, but I understand your question. The longer ellipse, as I've already said, shows the fragments that were left as a result of the impact of fragments of the projectile and they are deeper in the direction from which the shell came, because as a shell is flying toward the impact point there would be an angle there. And as a result of the explosion, the traces would be deeper and clearer from the direction from which the shell came, whereas on the opposite side the traces would be less visible. This would be the simpler explanation. And I still have no interpretation in my headset.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we check that the witness receives interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No I do. Now I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I now ask you, looking at this photograph, apparently the X1 ax is the ax which gives the direction from which the projectile arrived. Could you tell us, did it come from, to say so, from the upper part of the photograph or was the origin of fire to the lower part of the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in an idealised photograph, as we see it here, it's obvious that it comes from the bottom part of the photograph because you can see that the traces there are more visible and they are more dispersed away from the centre of the explosion. So the X1 ax is actually, that's -- it's coming from the direction of the bottom of the photograph, if I may put it that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So we're looking along the ax on which the projectile landed, being fired from our backs if we look at the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No -- well, actually, it came from my direction, if I can put it that way. Yes, right, from your backs as you are seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Everyone who's looking at the photograph in the same way as I do would find that it was fired from behind, landing on the photograph. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution tenders the marked exhibit --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the marked excerpt of the report would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P871, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P871 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we move to another exhibit may I put one question to the witness. Sir, you have explained the different ellipses, but I see above -- now the marking disappeared now. Can we have the marking back? I start already with my question. I see some markings in the road above the centre of the impact as you described. Can you -- have you any idea what is that marking indicating? There are some spots you haven't described yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Those points are, in fact, also traces left by the fragments of the shell, but you can see that they are closer to the centre of the explosion. Because, as I've already said, the traces are always more pronounced and deeper in the direction from which the shell came. And of course these are all traces of this mortar projectile, or rather, its fragments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you have an explanation why we see these little spots also in a kind of circle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that is the characteristic of the so-called rosetta that I've already mentioned that is left as a result of impact of a mortar projectile on a surface. When the fragments or shrapnel disperses, this is the shape that it would leave behind, but we also have to bear in mind the angle of descent at which this shell landed; and then we can determine how far these traces would spread out. But as I've already said, they're always longer and more pronounced on the side from which the projectile came. But it's also normal that traces would be seen on the other side, if I may put it that way, from the centre of the explosion. But that would then depend on the incoming angle of the shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Just for the clarity of the record, we are discussing now the little spots on the left side of the X1 marked by you and not as clearly visible on the right side of that X1. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one more question. The closer you look at the ellipse, closer to the centre of impact, the smaller, more narrow it is, whereas further away from it the ellipse gets broader. Is that how I have to understand this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct. It fans out. You understood that very well. It spreads in the shape of a fan, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 7 of 65 ter 10261 in the B/C/S version only. And if we could please focus on the lower photo marked number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, directing your attention to this bottom photo number 6, could you please explain how you used the equipment depicted in this photograph to determine the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: In this photograph you can see the traces marked. You can also see the centre of the explosion. That's where all these sticks meet. You can see the shapes of the ellipses, the smaller one and the larger one that fans out. You can also see that these two lateral sticks form a certain angle that we derived by connecting the outward poles of the longer ellipse with the centre of the explosion. And this central stick that goes towards the centre, it has some red colour on it, that is the central axis of the angle formed by these two other sticks. And at the same time, that would be the direction of the projectile. Now, beyond this you can see this measuring tape below the sticks which shows the direction north, and I believe there is an N there. Now, on the upper part of the photograph you can see a map of Sarajevo and the compass that is north-oriented and placed close to the location as best we could on the map. So this is what you can see in this photograph and this explains the method of the central axis, an illustration, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is this the same crater as we looked at in the previous photo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, it is the same crater but the photograph is taken from a different angle.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 10261 into evidence as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10261 receives number P872, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P865, page 15 of the B/C/S and page 8 of the English translation. The Prosecution requests that the document not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I'd like to direct your attention to the shelling on the 22nd of January, 1994, in Alipasino Polje. If I could please have page 8 of the English version and page 15 of the B/C/S. Do you recognise this as -- the document before you as the report you authored in relation to your investigation of the shelling on the 22nd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I wrote up this report together with my colleague, Borislav Stankov, late, who was at the time a forensic ballistics expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In this report you make observations about three projectile impacts. Could you explain to us what specific measurements you took during this investigation that allowed you to determine that two of the impacts were caused by an 82-millimetre mortar shell and one from 120-millimetre mortar shell?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: We used the usual method. We used the central axis method. We did the measurements, as I've already explained a moment ago, using those photographs. And we even found a stabilising fin in one of the craters, the 82-millimetre stabiliser. And the dimension of these -- the dimensions of these rosettas, or rather, these irregular ellipses corresponded to the second shell where we didn't find the stabilising fin but we could conclude that it was an 82-millimetre shell. And the third shell that landed near Rade Koncar Street was the result of a 120-millimetre shell impacting that ground there because the rosetta or the traces that we found on the surface were about 30 to 40 per cent larger than the traces that we found in Klare Cetkin Street. So it was really easy to establish what type of projectiles or what type of calibre they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the next page of the report in both versions. With respect to the one that you determined to be a 120-millimetre shell, exactly how much bigger was it in comparison to the two other ellipses according to your measurements here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, here you can see the measurements themselves and they speak for themselves. The 120-millimetre shell, the length of the axis was rather greater than the ones we found where the 82-millimetre shells impacted the ground. In other words, this second one even was 80- to 120 centimetres long and it spread out 3.20 by 4.80 metres - you can see that - as compared to the 80-millimetre shell. We can read it from the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to move on now and discuss with you the Markale investigation that you conducted on the 5th of February, 1994. Your discussion of this is on pages 30 to 48 of your statement. One of the exhibits that you comment upon is a video of the market. The Prosecution is again going to show you parts of this video and ask you for some additional comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, this video has been admitted as P864 and with your leave I'll ask Ms. Stewart to play the first 17 seconds of the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please continue playing to the 17th-second mark.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, which direction is the camera facing at this time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: It's facing the Marsala Tita Street. It's the southern side in relation to the market.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will now ask Ms. Stewart to play the video from the 6 minute, 39 second point and pause 20 seconds later at 6 minutes and 59 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, in the portion of the video that we just saw, what is depicted?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The central crater, the point of impact. You can see fragmentation traces, blood, flesh, and these three sticks that demonstrate the method used. You have the two lateral sticks and the white stick would be the central axis, so that should correspond to the direction from which the shell came.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you place these sticks on the crater during this crater analysis?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I and a colleague of mine, Hamdija Cavcic, we were at the on-site investigation performing the duties of ballistics experts there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, I am looking at the clock. We are already beyond the time where we usually take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a fine point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a good point. Then we turn into closed session for the witness to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Weber, I read there -- perhaps the witness could carefully listen as well - Mr. Sabljica, in the summary of your evidence, which by the way is not the evidence itself, Mr. Weber read that you had concluded that the projectiles had been fired from positions in Nedzarici. Reading your statement I see that you say that the projectiles originated from a westerly direction, that in that westerly direction Nedzarici was found. But I did not actually see that you said that they were fired from positions in Nedzarici, although they may well have been. Is that an accurate reflection of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, because the methods we used were not such that we could determine with precision the location from which a shell had been fired. So we never really specified the exact position and the troops that were there. Nedzarici was in that area, as it says in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but it could have come from that direction but further away than Nedzarici. You did not determine the distance the projectile had travelled; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could please return to Exhibit P864. During the break I asked Ms. Stewart to pause the video at the next portion which is 8 minutes and 33 seconds into the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, before you is a compass map and arrow. Could you please explain what these items show in this portion of the video.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: They show a map of Sarajevo, the location of Markale roughly speaking. The compass has been positioned in that area. And the map is -- direction was north. You can see that the compass is to the north and you can see that it's 18 degrees to the north/north-east from the location we assumed that the shell came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you use these specific items during your investigation to determine that the shell came from 18 degrees to the north/north-east?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. We always used a compass and a map in order to provide approximate bearings, approximate locations in the vicinity of the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please play this video for the next 12 seconds and pause at 8 minutes and 45 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is depicted on the screen before us at this point in the video?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The centre of the crater. This is the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you make your determination as to the direction of fire before all of the debris had been removed from the crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that you already have the lateral stakes there and also the main axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I will now ask Ms. Stewart to play the next 20 seconds of the video and pause at 9 minutes and 5 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the segment that we just saw there was some individuals in blue helmets cleaning away the debris from the crater. Who were these individuals?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: UNPROFOR members, the specialist team that would often go to on-site investigations when the town was shelled. These members were from the French Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And if we could play just another seven seconds of the video and pause at 9 minutes, 22 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we can just go back briefly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 36 of your statement you state that the stabiliser was found at the centre of the crater at a depth of 9 centimetres from the asphalt surface. You continue to state that the measured depth was from the top of the asphalt up until the last part of the stabiliser. Did you measure the stabiliser in the position that is depicted on the screen before us?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, those are the dimensions before it was taken out, before the stabiliser was taken out from the centre of the crater.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you measure the total depth of the crater after the stabiliser had been removed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I didn't do so personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to turn -- we're completed with the video. I'd like to turn to discuss some brief things with respect to sniping. On pages 60 and 61 of your statement you discuss how you went to four high-rise buildings on Lenjinova Street in 1996. Did you go to these buildings as part of a commission that was formed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, after the reintegration of Grbavica, after the peace agreement and as ordered by the investigative judge, an expert team went to the site to carry out an examination in the buildings in Lenjinova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who were the other members of this commission?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: They were experienced ballistics experts, colleagues of mine, the late Cavcic, the late Stankov, and the late Medjedovic. There were officials from the CSB police in Sarajevo and there was the investigative judge and myself and two forensic experts, Sanjin Hasanefendic, I believe, and I can't remember the name of the other person.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On page 61 of your statement you describe how these apartments looked, including the demolished partitions and conical openings. Did you find any ammunition or weapons in these apartments during this investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Naturally we didn't search all the flats, only some that were above the 10th floor. We found so-called sniper nests. That was the first time I had the opportunity of seeing something of that kind. There were these openings in the walls, these breaches that had been made in a professional manner. I read up about it later on and learned certain things about it. There were cartridges that were found, cartridges of bullets of various calibres. They were probably the cartridges of M76 semi-automatic rifles. There were M84 machine-guns that had been -- that had probably been used. We found sandbags that were used as protection for snipers. We compiled a report on this, photographed it, photographed everything, and sent all of this material for further processing.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the result of the commission?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: We visited those buildings mainly because in the course of the conflict in Sarajevo in particular all of our findings showed that this was an area from which we suspected that there were sniper shots on trams, on pedestrians who were walking around parts of the town that were under the ABiH. So according to our assessments, according to our methods that we used, we came to the conclusion that we had been quite precise in our assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weber. Mr. Lukic, are you ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I just need one minute to organise myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Meanwhile, Mr. Sabljica, you will be cross-examined now by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're all laymen here when it comes to the field that you are testifying about, so I do hope that you will use simple language when explaining certain matters to us and we will try to make good use of the investigations you have carried out. And perhaps you could provide us with more detailed explanations. Can we start now?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you started working in the MUP you had -- you didn't have much knowledge of the field of ballistics; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You learned about ballistics when you attended a six-month course and this course was provided by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's correct too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Although you have already testified about this, I'll just repeat this so that we can clear certain matters up. Your task was to determine the origin of fire, the type of shell fired, and the calibre of the shell in question; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't determine the distance?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, we didn't determine distances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the expression "origin of fire" is quite ambiguous in this context. I take it that you wanted to refer to the direction of the origin of fire, which from the follow-up question I think is what you meant to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 10 of your statement you say, it's line 24: We stated the area under the control of such and such an army only if we were a hundred per cent certain that no one else had positions there. Is it true that there was a confrontation line around the entire town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, you're quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that that confrontation line was wave-like, the entire line was wave-like?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's correct too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you worked as a ballistics expert in the MUP, did you receive any information from the 1st Corps of the ABiH about where their units were deployed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no. There was no such co-operation at my level.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know where the warehouses were, where the brigade staffs were of the 1st Corps of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I knew about certain places, but not for all of -- not about all of them. There are very few places I was aware of as a policeman and a citizen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Very briefly I'd like to have a look at 10347 [as interpreted], which is a 65 ter document. I would like to see it in the e-court system. It's a Prosecution exhibit and I will briefly ask you about it -- something about it when it comes up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record this is P858.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I didn't have time to include today's numbers to my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, I thought P858 was exhibit -- was 65 ter 10447 and this one is 10347.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, I quote 447, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say 447?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica -- [In English] Okay. That's it. [Interpretation] Mr. Sabljica, does this arrow that extends from the shell to the edge demonstrate the direction from which the shell came or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, this is just a way in which we marked where the central crater was located, the central crater in which the stabiliser is embedded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't need this photograph anymore. In the testimony you gave in other cases you explained the method you used to determine the direction of fire. And, amongst other things, you said the following in your statement on page 19: "A mortar shell, when it falls, its axis closes off an angle which is usually below 90 degrees. When it comes into contact with the surface and when it explodes, the shell fragments and you can see visible traces that spread out from the centre of the explosion in the direction from which the shell arrived."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter notes there is a lot of interference and the interpreter can't hear anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the interpreters tell us that there's a lot of interference and that they have difficulty in hearing you. Is there any paperwork --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably because of the paper --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which is touching upon the microphone?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will turn off the mike in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I apologise to the translators. [Interpretation] Could we have a look at 1D703 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you take a pencil and mark the centre of the explosion at the point of impact and the way in which the fragments are fanned out. Can you see this in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher would assist if the witness would make any markings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the centre of the explosion, I'll mark it with a C, and here we have the ellipse -- the ellipses here, given what I can see in the photograph. So this is a -- an idealised manner of depicting the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we save this as the next Defence exhibit marked as it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D703 as marked by the witness receives number D171, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could now see 1D697 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, could you mark the centre of the explosion in this photograph too and the ellipses that show the traces left when the shell exploded?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: This is the centre of the explosion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, before we continue I think one question should be put to the witness first. Until now you have explained to us how you measured the direction of the origin of fire if a shell landed on a surface -- on the ground. Apparently we now hear/see an impact of a projectile on a wall. Would the same theory and the same explanation apply to the impact of a projectile on a wall? That's the first question before we continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the case of a mortar shell there would be a rosette. If it's a projectile from a barrel, bore barrel, then it would be different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And would the rosette be explained in a way similar to a mortar shell that would have landed on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the principle is the same. If we are dealing with a mortar shell there's no difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Judge put some questions that I was going to put to you, but could you please now mark the ellipses for us in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When I -- when we have a look at this photograph would you draw the conclusion that the shell came from below?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, that wouldn't be logical. How would that be possible? If you have an opening in the wall, it must have hit the wall at a certain angle, that is more or less a right angle. That's common sense. But you can see how the shrapnel spread, so perhaps it was an angle of between 75 and 80 degrees. The circle seems to be a little more regular in relation to the ellipses when you're dealing with, for example, a shell that hits the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will just ask you about this because there were positions there and certain people suspect that the shell was fired from a lower level. Correct me if I'm wrong, but I can't see any shrapnel traces on the upper side on the facade. Can you? You're referring to the damage inflicted?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, you can see these traces here further above, but it's difficult to carry out an analysis on the basis of a photograph. You can see the opening made by the projectile that penetrated through to the flat. So the angle was over 15 degrees, for example, if we talk about someone who fired from a lower level, but the picture would be a lot clearer if we could go to the site. But what you're saying can't be excluded, but if you have a look at the photograph it wouldn't be logical to say that someone fired from a lower level and then managed to penetrate the wall in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying it was from down below but perhaps from the vicinity. But now I'd like us to concentrate on another incident that concerns the 1st of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- does this originate from any of the scheduled incidents or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You gave the 65 ter number but I do not know where it's taken from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's actually -- I don't know if I can mention the name of the witness, one of the witnesses who is coming soon brought this -- these pictures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, which is not a real answer to my question who brought it. I was more interested to know it is related to one of the scheduled incidents? Is it anything found on the spot of one of these scheduled incidents or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to check this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you would like to have this one admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you to Judge Fluegge, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I speak on his behalf. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Photograph 1D697 as marked by the witness receives D172, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. D172 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to the incidents that are the reason for you being here today. We have that clearly separated, but I don't know if this image is part of it. So let's move on to the 1st of June, 1993, the shelling of the football match in Dobrinja. You say: "I've looked at the photo documentation of the BH MUP of 20th November 1995 and the report of 24th November 1995." So this is not a mistake. This photograph and the reports were produced two and a half years after the incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's correct because the 1st -- on the 1st of June, 1993, I was not even in the MUP and we did this investigation after the signing of the Dayton Agreement pursuant to a request by the ICTY investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You signed this report and I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, is there any way to get on our screen what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have next session. It's page 29, lines 3 to 8, in B/C/S actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if it's photographs, I do not mind that much --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, this is from the statement of this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes, we are talking about the statement. Page?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 29 I had in B/C/S. One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it perhaps page 19?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have different lines, line 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see what I can find.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's about forensic investigation. I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is the corresponding page to the B/C/S page on the left side of the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which page are you in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] It's page 29 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Twenty-nine of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it is page 18 in English I am told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 18 in English, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it's 19.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or 19. Okay, the first -- the line numbers are not the same. Yes, it's page 18, line 40, and it goes to the next page, page 19 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I found it. I have inspected it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You tell us: "The forensic investigation was done on site with the help of a CSB forensic technician, Miralem Sarvan, and an authorised official of the crime department of the BH MUP, Enes Zeljkovic. Also present were the international criminal tribunal investigators, Jan van Hecke, an operative of the Sarajevo CSB, Mirsad Kucanin and witness Refik Sokolar. It was determined that the shell that fell on a Tarmac surface was an 82-millimetre shell." At the time when you prepared this report were you aware that there had already been a report on this incident made by UNPROFOR in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Unfortunately, no, I didn't know of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you questioned Dinko [Realtime transcript read in error "Vinko"] Bakal as a witness, whether you interviewed him? Because in this report that was prepared by the UN this person was mentioned as someone who claimed that it was a 60-millimetre shell, and according to him the BH Army had established that this was the calibre in question and taken away the fragments. Did you interview this man?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I have no idea who Dinko Bakal is and, among other things, I can mention it wasn't my job to interview any witnesses. I only did the work that I explained this morning, in other words, determining the direction of a shell, the patterns, the trace evidence, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall whether anyone interviewed Mr. Bakal?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I really don't know anything about that. If I did, I'd tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We now need exhibit -- actually, it was 10261 earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P872, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Lukic, my apologies. Your Honour, if you allow, the name of Mr. Dinko Bakal in the transcript is misrecorded. It says "Vinko Bakal." It should be "Dinko Bakal." Just to make sure everything is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just -- I'm a bit surprised. You're correcting a name of a person you say you've no idea who he is. That is -- now you say it's not Vinko but it's Dinko.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the gentleman heard how I pronounced it. That's why he was able to [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is you pronounced it as "Dinko," it was transcribed as "Vinko" --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and that was corrected. Now I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, P872 - and you can see what it is, it's a -- it's this report, the photo file - on page 2 in the B/C/S, which is probably page 3 in e-court, yes, we need page 3. And that's page 4 in the English version. The top paragraph on this page of the report -- or actually the sixth paragraph and that's the second tab begins with the words "the position of the central crater ..." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It says: "The position of the central crater on the Tarmac surface created by the explosion of an artillery shell was fixed based on an arch section in relation to the stairwell (on the eastern side of the parking-lot) and a known length of the segment, which is 4 metres (and on the eastern edge of the parking-lot) ..." A little later I will ask you to depict this paragraph -- to make a sketch on paper if possible because it's really difficult for me to follow this as it is. Also, in this same report it says that this shell had come from the south-east; correct? We can see that on the following page of the B/C/S version. Could we please pull that up. And that's on the following page in the English version as well. Is this the direction that you determined, 110 degrees from the north?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that is the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us briefly how you determined the direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I used the same method that I described earlier, the main axis method and using the compass and the city plan. So that's the way we determined the direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But on this occasion you did not try to establish the incoming angle of the projectile, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not establish the source of fire either, did you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, incoming angle is again an ambiguous expression. I take it that you want to refer to the angle of descent? Because the incoming angle could also be to north or south or west or east, but the angle of descent is the vertical angle and that is what you refer to, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. Let's try to use as clearly our words so that no confusion can result.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sabljica, you did not establish the source of fire or the place from which the shell was fired either, did you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, of course not. That was impossible based on the physical evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now pull up in e-court 1D696.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether this photograph was taken on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, it was and I am in the photograph too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you establish now - and do you agree with me - that according to this photograph bearing north is a bit to the left of the house at the foot of Mojmilo hill that we see in the background here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately in the direction of this gentleman who is on top of this van and that house behind him, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D696 receives number D173, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Lukic, just for my understanding, it's very difficult in a two-dimensional photograph to find where north is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because if you're from that group of people would make -- well, let's say from the heads of the people to the right to the feet of the man standing on the car, then on the photograph north would be to the left of the photograph. But you also could think of some depth and then you're talking about the house. I see three houses before Mojmilo hill, isn't it? But I take it you want to refer to the most -- the one most to the left. But even then I can draw your -- a lot of lines and still do not know what north is. Now, not to say that it is not important and that it cannot be established, but not on the basis of this photograph. That's my problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Being semi-blind I saw only one building on this picture but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, yes, you know that the Chamber has to keep both eyes open, all three of us, which makes six eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- should I clarify with this witness from which position he thinks that -- I was thinking from the position of the man who was standing here and taking the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My problem is that on a two-dimensional photograph you can't bring in any depth. You would need a three-dimensional photograph for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore if --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We did have some three-dimensional photographs but we were informed that we cannot use it here in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we should find ways that we are able to do it. If that is a request, I certainly will follow it up with the -- but at this moment the witness has been asked questions. How we evaluate his answers is a different matter, but the document now is in evidence. I just wanted to let you know -- is it in evidence, by the way? Yes, I admitted it. It was admitted. I just wanted to share with you my concerns about what you can see and what you could deduce from the witness's answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My colleague Judge Fluegge included in your question, although I didn't see it, I only saw that could you establish on the -- according to this photograph, but that you wanted to take as a starting point the point where apparently the photographer has -- yes, that was not part of your question, but I better understand it now. If I made a mistake, which is well possible, then I'll correct myself. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Everybody makes mistakes, even Judges sometimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I use the time to deal with a totally different matter --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. While waiting until the curtains are up I put on the record that the redacted statement of Witness Rose was admitted as P736. The unredacted statement had been previously been MFI'd as P728 and accordingly P728 is vacated. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will now briefly have a look at a video. I have to say we don't have a transcript for the video. We will only view a one-minute extract and perhaps we could have a look at it twice so that the interpreters can interpret it. As I have said, we don't have a transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, you know that playing it twice is a procedure which we apply even in the presence of a transcript. We'll play it for the first time and then we'll ask the advice of our interpreters to see whether they think that without a transcript that the speed of speech is such that they possibly can translate the second round.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we first look at it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask Ms. Stewart to play video marked as V000-3497. That's video from 18th September 2001 and we need time 1.55 to 2.55.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid this is wrong video. We need one with Mr. Hogan on it, that's 3497.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Certainly this is not a video of September 2001. Therefore, we -- apparently you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm using help of Ms. Stewart so we didn't have time to prepare --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This seems to the extent I know who Mr. Hogan is, it seems to be closer to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can we play it now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Mr. Hogan: Could you please show me by standing in the spot where one of the posts for the goal-posts was located on the 1st of June, 1993. "Could you now please show me by standing on the spot where the second goal-post at this end of the parking-lot was located on the 1st of June, 1993, to the best of your recollection."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we'll first have to ask the booths -- as a matter of fact, there seems to be no B/C/S/English problem because it is translated already. So therefore it's mainly the French booth and I'll switch to channel 5 now to hear whether they were able to translate in the second round. Mr. Lukic, the French interpreters think that they could translate if we play it for a second time. We have English and B/C/S already. Of course, I would like to invite the English and the B/C/S interpreters to tell us whether the translation as given in the video is accurate, yes or no, because that could be a second source of confusion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters in the English booth note that the interpretation is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have confirmation that the interpretation is accurate. Let's play it for a second time and then we have a full record, it being translated by the French booth as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "Mr. Hogan: Could you please show me by standing in the spot where one of the posts for the goal-posts was located on the 1st of June, 1993. "Could you now please show me by standing on the spot where the second goal-post at this end of the parking-lot was located on the 1st of June, 1993, to the best of your recollection."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you agree, Mr. Sabljica, that the man with a crutch covered the distance of about 3 metres to show how wide the goal-posts were apart?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I can agree that that's approximately what it is. I believe these are the hand-ball goals.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. And you could also note that behind Mr. Hogan in the background, behind Mr. Hogan and the man with a crutch, we could see the monument erected in memorial of the people who were killed there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I could see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please show a much shorter clip, video-clip. We don't need audio. We just need V000-2479. We just need a few seconds beginning from 2 hours, 8 minutes, and 20 seconds, to 2 hours, 8 minutes, and 26 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show it one more time, please, and would you please just pay attention to the Volkswagen where a small goal can be seen, much smaller than a hand-ball goal.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We have interference in our headsets and it's very difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, there's interference again in the headsets of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We believe it's of a technical nature. It has nothing to do with what's going on in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I then ask the specific attention of the technicians to this interference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see in this photograph any traces of blood that there was someone injured here and probably dragged across?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, what you can see in front of the Volkswagen and the blue car, and there is a kind of line there, a curved line, you mean that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This is a photograph, or rather, a video-clip from one of the BH TV stations from that day, and we're going to deal with this in more detail. I can't find the number now. I should show you a photograph. Please bear with me. Could we now pull up 1D705 and show it on the monitors. This is the playground in Dobrinja. Can you recognise it? And we can see the goal-post there and these are, I would say, hand-ball posts.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I do see that it is a playground and that it is in Dobrinja, but I'm not sure that that is that particular playground because I don't know how well you know Dobrinja but there are many areas that look similar to one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you know that this playground was built and the goal-posts were actually placed there when Dobrinja settlement was being built?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know anything about that because I lived in a different part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Were you aware that Mr. Richard Higgs had visited this site with OTP representatives?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about Mr. Higgs. I only know what I did with Mr. van Hecke, what we did together.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this photograph, please. And although we didn't hear much detail from this witness, but we will need it in our work and we will be using it again and I believe that the Prosecutor will not object because it's from their source.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution wouldn't oppose marking it for identification just so we have a clear record of its use later. However, based on the foundation laid by this witness it's really unclear as to what's being depicted. So I accept that counsel may use this later in [overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] It marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I agree. And I can give the V number from which this photo was taken. It's V000-7585.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it is still from that video.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number this photograph would receive, it to be marked for identification would be ... ?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D175, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D175 is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now pull up in e-court 1D662.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is Richard Higgs' report as you can see, and it was prepared on the 12th of February, 2002. We need page 7, second paragraph in the English, and page 8, the first paragraph in the B/C/S version. What you can see here that the first paragraph reads: "At the request of the Tribunal I visited the site with Mr. Chester Stamp and examined the two craters in question. The two craters have been filled in with a red substance and to a degree have made my -- any detailed analysis now impossible. However, enough of the crater is still present to draw some conclusions." This is a description of the same incident. Now, can you explain how it was that Mr. Higgs located -- identified two craters, whereas you found only one?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, I do. I can explain it. I -- it is possible that we were taken to a location where this different incident occurred. Where we went there was only one crater. Now, it is possible also that Mr. Higgs was taken to another location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I already asked you at the beginning related to this incident whether you knew anything about the UNPROFOR report immediately following the incident, and in this report too it was mentioned that there were two shells that landed on a hard surface. And then it brackets it says it's macadam. So where you went and where you investigated there was only a crater -- one crater.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, and that's what we said in our report and the other one had fallen on earth, on soft earth, and that place had already changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to talk about the incident at Alipasino Polje of 22nd January 1994. You told us in your report, do you recall, that on this occasion you found two shells, two 82-millimetre shells, but that you could not find a stabiliser fin, but that you did find a stabiliser fin of a 122 -- 20-millimetre [as interpreted] shell that had fallen off a roof-top. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct, would you know, that Mr. Tuzovic in his report mentioned that there were three shells that struck on this particular occasion?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, and we too mentioned the third shell that landed on soft ground at Rade Koncar Trg, but it's also true that we found these two and we did find the stabiliser fin and we assume -- of 120-millimetre shell and we assume that it must have fallen from the roof-top because it couldn't have been otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you would guide us to the relevant page then it's easier for us to follow the evidence. 22nd of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's English page 29, line 25. In B/C/S it's page 42.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's then see about -- two 82-millimetres and then the 120-millimetre appears. Because you summarised it as a --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My mistake. My mistake. It's different section. I asked the question about English version page 19, line 40 to 44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look. Yes, where you said but that you did find a stabiliser fin of 122-millimetre shell, which apparently seems to be 120-millimetre shell, that had fallen off a roof-top, whether he remembers that answer. What I found until now is that the witness would have said: "Except for one shell for which allegedly it was said that it fell on the roof and that has 120-millimetre calibre." So he didn't say that it fell from a roof-top. He said that it fell allegedly as it was said on a roof -- or is it somewhere else, Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We should continue on page 29.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where we were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now go back to 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, are we still in the same -- we're still in G6. Yes, 29 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see a 120-millimetre shell on line 15 --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we have to switch to line 30 in English, top of the page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Line 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the first row --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see -- yes, one second --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "While this gentleman says," that's the portion. In Mr. Tuzovic's report it was erroneously stated that two 120-millimetre shells fell, and the previous page, toward the end of page 29, Mr. Sabljica claims that in total three shells landed, two 82-millimetre shells hit Cetkinska Street and one 120-millimetre shell landed which landed in Klara Cetkin Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's something different from what you put to the witness first, but please ask him the questions you have in your mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I confused and I was maybe rushing too much but I think that gentleman can. My point was that I just wanted to actually point out different reports on the same event done by the Sarajevo police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that point is clear. We haven't seen the other one. We have the statement of this witness now which says that the other report --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- erroneously stated that there were two 120-millimetre shells. Which, Mr. Lukic, for me mainly means that if there are two different reports that either one is wrong or the other one is wrong or both are wrong. The only thing is they can't be right --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unless -- well, unless -- I have not seen that report so I don't know where the problem really lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 29th page, 39th row we have a question. Mr. Sabljica was asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 39 you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, 29th page, 39th row -- line.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sabljica, can you confirm, is it acceptable for an investigation team that goes to visit a site, especially in connection to such serious incidents with serious consequences, is it acceptable for such a team to provide such blanket statements that haven't been verified? Is this acceptable? Can this being allowed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, it's not acceptable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have for the sake of the interpreters page 29 on the screen in English and the corresponding page in B/C/S. I think you were referring to --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] -- I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- to line 39. It's on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I should have read out the answer provided by Mr. Sabljica, which was: "It is unacceptable and I can't be allowed." And today we see that his position is the same because he provided the same kind of answer to the question that I read out. So we know what his position is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, can you confirm that, what Mr. Lukic just put to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I stand by the findings that I and my colleague Stanko arrived at. And Mr. Tuzovic, according to -- on the basis of his training, was a forensic expert. He couldn't have had more experience when it came to ballistics than we had. Such mistakes are unacceptable but such mistakes were made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I understand you well, "by others" you mean to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. When I say it's unacceptable, it's unacceptable from the point of view of the rules that guided the service at the time and from the point of view of police practice. I think that Mr. Tuzovic made some mistakes here. He didn't consult anyone when it was necessary to submit the full report. He didn't consult anyone and wait for our findings which are more authoritative in my opinion. According to the police structure our service was a more senior service. He was no more than an assistant in the field in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. If we could now see P865 in the e-court system. Later we'll have to go back to this document when I try to find the pages, but I'll continue with my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you seen a report that was compiled in relation to this incident?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, I had the opportunity of reading the full report not in connection with preparations for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that such a report on an on-site investigation doesn't provide much information?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: From my point of view I would think that the report was a correct one. But as for everything else, all other matters, I'm not in a position to comment on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As for the photographs taken in relation to the incident, would you say that it was done in an appropriate manner?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Well, it was done on the basis of certain basic criteria, but you can see that some reports were more professional. A forensic technician has to take photographs of the site in question. That is part of the tasks that he has to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But we do agree that three shells struck?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in my report and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now just have a look at a map 1D664.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if you could mark something on the map once I've put my question to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Madam Registrar reminded us that this document is under seal. She has already instructed that it not be shown to the public -- the previous one. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think it's necessary to enlarge the part where it says "Alipasino Polje" so that we can see it more clearly. No -- [In English] That's on the right-hand side. Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you now take a marker and mark with numbers, if you know anything about this, the order in which the shells fell. And if that isn't possible just mark the sites they fell at.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'll try to mark the sites but I can't mark the order. I didn't speak to the witnesses about this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: I'll try. I think it's in this part of Alipasino Polje. I think it's called square. Now that would be the wider area. Do you want me to mark it with a letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have a number or some kind now, number 6.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes, that's number 6 there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Two shells impacted at that site?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the third one?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: The third one fell behind the buildings and struck soft ground in the park. That was the 120-millimetre one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that site with a triangle?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The speakers are frequently overlapping now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please make a small pause between question and answer; and you between answer and question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that this witness is very disciplined and he follows, but probably I am jumping.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this occasion too you didn't measure the azimuth. You didn't know what the azimuth was in relation to the direction of fire, the direction the shells came from?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: No, that's correct, we didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the photographs taken in this case -- amongst the photographs taken you can't see any photographs of the point of impact of the shell that fell in the Rade Koncar square and the park?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA
utterances.text: That's correct, between Klare Cetkin Street and the square, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
